detail.zh: 照这个读法，守规矩不是傻，但你也没有义务做唯一守规矩的人——解决办法是执法，而不是英雄主义。霍布斯在别处也论证过，一旦存在共同权力，背约就违背理性。代价是：等待裁判，可能变成随波逐流的借口。

quote.en: For he that performeth first, has no assurance the other will performe after; because the bonds of words are too weak to bridle mens ambition, avarice, anger, and other Passions, without the feare of some coerceive Power
quote.zh: For he that performeth first, has no assurance the other will performe after; because the bonds of words are too weak to bridle mens ambition, avarice, anger, and other Passions, without the feare of some coerceive Power

label.en: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, ch. XIV
label.zh: 霍布斯《利维坦》第十四章

claim.en: Through Socrates at his trial I argued that a good man does not weigh his chances of living or dying, but asks only whether what he does is right or wrong.
claim.zh: 我借受审的苏格拉底之口论证：一个好人不去权衡自己生死的机会，只问自己所做的事是对是错。

detail.en: These are Plato's words for Socrates, defending his life before a jury, and carrying them to a lost contract is our application. Where Mencius ranks one good above another, Socrates declines to put winning on the scale at all. The cost is that he paid with his life, and most people who refuse to cut corners have families who did not choose that price.
detail.zh: 这是柏拉图借苏格拉底之口、在陪审团前为自己辩护时说的话，把它用到一份丢掉的合同上，是我们的引申。孟子是把一种善排在另一种善之上，苏格拉底则干脆不把输赢放上天平。代价是：他为此付出了生命，而多数拒绝走捷径的人，身后都有并未选择承担这一代价的家人。

quote.en: a man who is good for anything ought not to calculate the chance of living or dying; he ought only to consider whether in doing anything he is doing right or wrong—acting the part of a good man or of a bad.
quote.zh: a man who is good for anything ought not to calculate the chance of living or dying; he ought only to consider whether in doing anything he is doing right or wrong—acting the part of a good man or of a bad.

origin.zh: 雅典，约公元前 390 年代

label.en: Plato, Apology (28b), trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 柏拉图《申辩篇》（28b），乔伊特 英译

claim.en: I held that being right does not wait on numbers: a man more right than his neighbours is already a majority of one.
claim.zh: 我认为，对错不取决于人数：一个比邻人更正确的人，本身就已经是一个人的多数。

detail.en: He wrote it about withdrawing support from a government that upheld slavery, a far graver wrong than cutting corners at work, and the transfer is ours. Kant's test asks what everyone could do; Thoreau simply refuses to let the count matter. The weakness is that the same confidence serves anyone sure they are right, including people who are wrong.
detail.zh: 他是在主张撤回对一个维护奴隶制的政府的支持时写下这句话的，那远比职场上走捷径严重，这种移用是我们做的。康德的检验问的是人人能否这样做；梭罗则干脆不让人数起作用。弱点在于：同样的自信，任何自认为正确的人都可以用，包括错了的人。

quote.en: Moreover, any man more right than his neighbors constitutes a majority of one already.
quote.zh: Moreover, any man more right than his neighbors constitutes a majority of one already.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1849 年

label.en: Henry David Thoreau, "Civil Disobedience" (1849)
label.zh: 梭罗〈论公民的不服从〉（1849）

claim.en: I told myself never to count anything as profitable that would make me break my word, lose my self-respect, or need walls and veils to hide.
claim.zh: 我告诫自己：凡是会让我背弃诺言、丧失廉耻，或需要墙壁和帷幕来掩藏的东西，都不要算作好处。

detail.en: These are private notes to himself, and applying them to an industry's habits is our reading. They give a quick test for any corner: would you cut it in the open? The cost is real, since Marcus wrote as an emperor who could afford to lose a deal, and the person losing bids may not be able to.
detail.zh: 这是他写给自己的私人笔记，把它用到一个行业的惯例上，是我们的读法。它给每一条捷径提供了一个简单的检验：你敢不敢当众这样做？代价是真实的：马可写这些话时是一位皇帝，丢一笔交易无伤大雅，而丢标的人未必承受得起。

quote.en: Never esteem of anything as profitable, which shall ever constrain thee either to break thy faith, or to lose thy modesty; to hate any man, to suspect, to curse, to dissemble, to lust after anything, that requireth the secret of walls or veils.
quote.zh: Never esteem of anything as profitable, which shall ever constrain thee either to break thy faith, or to lose thy modesty; to hate any man, to suspect, to curse, to dissemble, to lust after anything, that requireth the secret of walls or veils.

label.en: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, Book III, trans. Meric Casaubon
label.zh: 马可·奥勒留《沉思录》第三卷，卡索邦 英译

claim.en: I argued that when others break the rules of justice, their example both tempts a man and gives him a reason to follow, since holding back alone would make him the dupe of his own integrity. That is why I held that people need magistrates to enforce justice.
claim.zh: 我论证过，当别人违反正义的规则时，他们的榜样既诱惑一个人，也给了他跟随的理由，因为独自克制只会让他被自己的正直所愚弄。正因如此，我认为人们需要官长来强制维护正义。

detail.en: Hume was explaining why societies set up magistrates, not advising anyone to cheat, and applying it to one industry is our step. The strongest objection comes from his own conclusion: he treats the pull as a reason to build enforcement, which leaves open what one person should do while the referee is still missing.
detail.zh: 休谟是在解释社会为何要设立执法者，而不是劝人作弊；把它用到某个行业上是我们的引申。最有力的反驳来自他自己的结论：他把这种拉力当作建立执法的理由，却没有说在裁判缺席时，一个人自己该怎么做。

quote.en: Your example both pushes me forward in this way by imitation, and also affords me a new reason for any breach of equity, by shewing me, that I should be the cully of my integrity, if I alone should impose on myself a severe restraint amidst the licentiousness of others.
quote.zh: Your example both pushes me forward in this way by imitation, and also affords me a new reason for any breach of equity, by shewing me, that I should be the cully of my integrity, if I alone should impose on myself a severe restraint amidst the licentiousness of others.

label.en: David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book III, Part II, Section VII
label.zh: 休谟《人性论》第三卷第二章第七节

claim.en: I held that when a country's very survival is at stake, questions of justice, mercy or shame must give way, and the only course is the one that keeps it alive and free.
claim.zh: 我认为，当国家的存亡本身受到威胁时，正义与否、仁慈与否、光彩与否都必须让路，唯一的道路是让它存续并保持自由的那一条。

detail.en: He was advising citizens who counsel their country, not spies; the extension is ours. The cost is that everyone who has ever betrayed a state has believed, or claimed, they were saving it — the standard has no way to tell them apart in advance.
detail.zh: 他是在给为国家出谋划策的公民提建议，不是给间谍；延伸是我们的推论。代价是：每一个背叛过国家的人都相信或声称自己在拯救它——这个标准无法事先把他们区分开来。

quote.en: when the entire safety of our country is at stake, no consideration of what is just or unjust, merciful or cruel, praiseworthy or shameful, must intervene. On the contrary, every other consideration being set aside, that course alone must be taken which preserves the existence of the country and maintains its liberty.
quote.zh: when the entire safety of our country is at stake, no consideration of what is just or unjust, merciful or cruel, praiseworthy or shameful, must intervene. On the contrary, every other consideration being set aside, that course alone must be taken which preserves the existence of the country and maintains its liberty.

label.en: Niccolò Machiavelli, Discourses on Livy, Book III, ch. 41, trans. Ninian Hill Thomson
label.zh: 马基雅维利《论李维》第三卷第四十一章，汤姆森 英译

claim.en: I counted among the poisons that kill a commonwealth the doctrine that every private man may judge for himself what is good and evil.
claim.zh: 我把每个私人都可以自行判断善恶的学说，列为致使国家衰亡的毒药之一。

detail.en: Hobbes wrote after a civil war fought between people each sure they were saving England. The cost is that his answer leaves no remedy against a sovereign who is the one heading for disaster.
detail.zh: 霍布斯写作于一场内战之后——交战双方都确信自己在拯救英格兰。代价是：如果走向灾难的正是主权者本身，他的回答没有给出任何补救。

quote.en: I observe the Diseases of a Common-wealth, that proceed from the poyson of seditious doctrines; whereof one is, "That every private man is Judge of Good and Evill actions."
quote.zh: I observe the Diseases of a Common-wealth, that proceed from the poyson of seditious doctrines; whereof one is, "That every private man is Judge of Good and Evill actions."

label.en: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, ch. XXIX
label.zh: 霍布斯《利维坦》第二十九章

claim.en: Through the Laws speaking to Socrates in the Crito, I argued that a citizen must either persuade the city it is wrong or do what it orders. Socrates, condemned to death, chose to stay rather than escape.
claim.zh: 我借《克力同篇》中法律对苏格拉底说的话论证：公民要么说服城邦它错了，要么服从它的命令。被判死刑的苏格拉底选择留下，而不是逃走。

detail.en: By this standard, working against your country in secret is ruled out — not because it is never right, but because it skips persuasion. The cost is that persuasion can be impossible when the state hides what it is doing.
detail.zh: 照这个标准，暗中对抗自己的国家是被排除的——不是因为它永远不对，而是因为它跳过了说服。代价是：当国家隐瞒自己所做的事情时，说服可能根本无从谈起。

quote.en: whether in battle or in a court of law, or in any other place, he must do what his city and his country order him; or he must change their view of what is just
quote.zh: whether in battle or in a court of law, or in any other place, he must do what his city and his country order him; or he must change their view of what is just

origin.zh: 雅典，约公元前 4 世纪 60 年代

label.en: Plato, Crito (51b–c), trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 柏拉图《克力同篇》（51b–c），乔伊特 英译

claim.en: I taught that a ruler is served by never deceiving him and by opposing him to his face.
claim.zh: 我教导说，侍奉君主，不可欺骗他，而要当面直言冒犯他。

detail.en: Read today, a loyal dissenter speaks up rather than works in the dark. The cost is that open opposition is easy to punish; this standard asks for a courage that secret action was invented to avoid.
detail.zh: 放到今天来读，忠诚的异议者会站出来发声，而不是在暗处行动。代价是：公开反对很容易遭到惩罚；这个标准要求的勇气，正是秘密行动想要回避的。

quote.en: Tsze-lu asked how a ruler should be served. The Master said, 'Do not impose on him, and, moreover, withstand him to his face.'
quote.zh: 子路問事君，子曰：「勿欺也，而犯之。」

label.en: Confucius, Analects 14.23, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《论语·宪问》14.23，理雅各 英译

claim.en: I listed using a state's own subjects as spies among the means a state may never use, even in war, because such treacherous methods destroy the trust that any later peace needs.
claim.zh: 我把让本国臣民充当间谍列为国家即使在战争中也绝不可使用的手段，因为这类背信的手段会摧毁日后和平所需要的信任。

detail.en: Kant was writing about states using spies, not citizens spying on their own state; the inference is ours: if secret betrayal corrodes trust between nations, it corrodes it within one too. The cost is that his framework offers dissenters little beyond public argument.
detail.zh: 康德讨论的是国家使用间谍，而不是公民刺探自己的国家；推论是我们的：如果秘密背叛会侵蚀国与国之间的信任，它同样会侵蚀一国之内的信任。代价是：除了公开论辩，他的框架几乎没有给异议者留下别的办法。

quote.en: Among these forbidden means are to be reckoned the appointment of Subjects to act as spies
quote.zh: Among these forbidden means are to be reckoned the appointment of Subjects to act as spies

label.en: Immanuel Kant, The Metaphysics of Morals, Doctrine of Right, §57, trans. W. Hastie
label.zh: 康德《道德形而上学·法权论》第 57 节，黑斯蒂 英译

claim.en: I held that when a ruler pursues measures gravely harmful to the public, or reaches beyond his legal bounds, it is allowable to resist and depose him, even though the law would call it rebellion.
claim.zh: 我认为，当统治者推行对公众极其有害的措施，或越出法律界限时，反抗并废黜他是可以允许的，尽管法律会把这称为叛乱。

detail.en: Hume meant open resistance by the people and the other parts of a mixed constitution, not one person acting in secret; using it to defend a spy or leaker is ours. He also insisted elsewhere that such cases are rare and that obedience is the rule, so the weakness is that he gives no way to tell, in the moment, who has judged rightly.
detail.zh: 休谟说的是人民和混合政体中其他部分的公开反抗，而不是一个人暗中行事；用它来为间谍或泄密者辩护是我们的推论。他在别处也坚持，这种情形很少见，服从才是常规；所以弱点是：他没有给出办法，让人在当下分辨谁的判断是对的。

quote.en: Not only where the chief magistrate enters into measures, in themselves, extremely pernicious to the public, but even when he would encroach on the other parts of the constitution, and extend his power beyond the legal bounds, it is allowable to resist and dethrone him; though such resistance and violence may, in the general tenor of the laws, be deemed unlawful and rebellious.
quote.zh: Not only where the chief magistrate enters into measures, in themselves, extremely pernicious to the public, but even when he would encroach on the other parts of the constitution, and extend his power beyond the legal bounds, it is allowable to resist and dethrone him; though such resistance and violence may, in the general tenor of the laws, be deemed unlawful and rebellious.

label.en: David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book III, Part II, §X
label.zh: 大卫·休谟《人性论》第三卷第二部分第十节

claim.en: I held that laws must be obeyed because they are laws, not because each person judges them just, since telling the people that the laws are unjust is dangerous.
claim.zh: 我认为，法律之所以必须服从，是因为它们是法律，而不是因为每个人都认为它们公正；因为对民众说法律不公正，是危险的。

detail.en: Pascal's fragment is about domestic peace, not espionage, and his tone is debated: some read it as sincere counsel, others as a sceptic's bleak observation. Applying it to someone who spies on their own country is ours. The cost is that it gives no exit at all from a state that really is unjust.
detail.zh: 帕斯卡的这则断想关乎国内的安宁，不涉及间谍，而且其语气有争议：有人读作真诚的劝告，也有人读作怀疑论者冷峻的观察。把它用到监视本国的人身上是我们的推论。代价是：面对一个确实不公正的国家，它完全没有留出出路。

quote.en: It is dangerous to say to the people that the laws are not just, for men obey them only because they think them just. Therefore it is necessary to say at the same time that they must be obeyed because they are laws, as superiors must be obeyed, not because they are just, but because they are superiors.
quote.zh: It is dangerous to say to the people that the laws are not just, for men obey them only because they think them just. Therefore it is necessary to say at the same time that they must be obeyed because they are laws, as superiors must be obeyed, not because they are just, but because they are superiors.

label.en: Blaise Pascal, Thoughts (Pensées), trans. C. Kegan Paul
label.zh: 帕斯卡《思想录》，凯根·保罗 英译

claim.en: I held that a wise man keeps his judgement free within, while outwardly following the laws and customs of his time. I pointed to Socrates, who would not save his life by disobeying even an unjust magistrate.
claim.zh: 我认为，智者在内心保持判断的自由，在外则遵从当时的法律与习俗。我以苏格拉底为例：即便面对不公正的官员，他也不肯以违抗来保全性命。

detail.en: This gives the 'obey' half of the Laws' choice its own reason: thought is free, so action need not rebel; applying it to spying is ours. Some readers take Montaigne's conservatism as partly ironic, so the reading is contested. The cost is that it leaves the free mind with no outlet but silence when the state is heading for disaster.
detail.zh: 这为《克力同》中法律给出的选择里服从那一半提供了另一种理由：思想是自由的，所以行动不必反叛；把它用到间谍问题上是我们的推论。有些读者认为蒙田的保守带有几分反讽，因此这一解读有争议。代价是：当国家走向灾难时，自由的心灵除了沉默别无出路。

quote.en: a wise man, within, ought to withdraw and retire his soul from the crowd, and there keep it at liberty and in power to judge freely of things; but as to externals, absolutely to follow and conform himself to the fashion of the time.
quote.zh: a wise man, within, ought to withdraw and retire his soul from the crowd, and there keep it at liberty and in power to judge freely of things; but as to externals, absolutely to follow and conform himself to the fashion of the time.

label.en: Michel de Montaigne, Essays, "Of Custom, and that we should not easily change a law received", trans. Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》〈论习俗及不可轻易改变已有之法〉，科顿 英译，黑兹利特 编

claim.en: Through Socrates I argued that the best-governed and most peaceful city is the one whose rulers least want to rule, and the worst is the one whose rulers want it most.
claim.zh: 我借苏格拉底之口论证过，治理得最好、最安定的城邦，是统治者最不愿统治的城邦；最糟的，是统治者最渴望统治的城邦。

detail.en: Taken today, eagerness is a warning sign rather than a credential. The cost is practical: in any system where office must be sought, the reluctant rarely stand, so the rule can leave power to exactly the people it distrusts.
detail.zh: 放到今天来看，急切是一个警示，而不是资格。代价很实际：在任何需要主动争取职位的制度里，不情愿的人很少参选，于是这条规律可能恰恰把权力留给了它不信任的人。

quote.en: the State in which the rulers are most reluctant to govern is always the best and most quietly governed, and the State in which they are most eager, the worst.
quote.zh: the State in which the rulers are most reluctant to govern is always the best and most quietly governed, and the State in which they are most eager, the worst.

label.en: Plato, Republic, Book VII (520d), trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 柏拉图《理想国》第七卷（520d），乔伊特 英译

claim.en: We teach that the realm cannot be won by grasping: whoever tries to seize it spoils it, and whoever grips it loses it.
claim.zh: 我们教导说，天下不能靠攫取而得：强取者败坏它，紧握者失去它。

detail.en: This is less a ban on ambition than a prediction about it — the wanting itself distorts what is wanted. The cost is that the text offers no procedure: it tells you who will fail, not who should be chosen instead.
detail.zh: 这与其说是禁止野心，不如说是对野心的预言——想要本身就会扭曲所想要的东西。代价是：这段文字没有提供任何程序；它告诉你谁会失败，却没说该选谁。

quote.en: If any one should wish to get the kingdom for himself, and to effect this by what he does, I see that he will not succeed. The kingdom is a spirit-like thing, and cannot be got by active doing. He who would so win it destroys it; he who would hold it in his grasp loses it.
quote.zh: 將欲取天下而為之，吾見其不得已。天下神器，不可為也，為者敗之，執者失之。

origin.zh: 中国，约公元前 4 世纪

label.en: Laozi, Tao Te Ching, ch. 29, trans. James Legge
label.zh: 《道德经》第二十九章，理雅各 英译

claim.en: I am the book of Zhuangzi: offered high office, my master answered with a sacred tortoise, honoured on an altar but dead, and chose to stay alive in the mud. I tell it as a story of refusing office, not a theory of who should rule.
claim.zh: 我是《庄子》：有人请庄子做高官，他以一只神龟作答，那龟被供在庙堂之上却早已死去，而他宁愿活着在泥里拖着尾巴。我讲的是拒绝官职的故事，而不是谁该统治的理论。

detail.en: It is a story about refusing, not a theory of who should govern; and the refusal assumes you can afford a quiet life in the mud. The cost is that if everyone wise follows the tortoise, the altar is left to those who want it.
detail.zh: 这是一个关于拒绝的故事，而不是关于谁该治理的理论；而且这种拒绝预设了你负担得起在泥里自在的生活。代价是：如果所有明智的人都效法那只龟，庙堂就留给了想要它的人。

quote.en: Now would this tortoise rather be dead and have its remains venerated, or be alive and wagging its tail in the mud?
quote.zh: 此龜者，寧其死爲留骨而貴乎？寧其生而曳尾於塗中乎？

origin.zh: 中国，约公元前 4 世纪

label.en: Zhuangzi, ch. 17 "Autumn Floods", trans. Herbert A. Giles
label.zh: 《庄子·秋水》，翟理斯 英译

claim.en: I argued that the striving for more power is not a defect of some people but what all life does: the will to power is the will to live.
claim.zh: 我论证过，追求更多权力的冲动不是某些人的缺陷，而是一切生命所为：权力意志就是求生的意志。

detail.en: Read this way, the honest question is what a person's will to power aims at, not whether they have one. The cost is that the framework gives no brake: it explains ambition without telling you how to stop it from trampling others.
detail.zh: 这样读，诚实的问题是一个人的权力意志指向什么，而不是他有没有。代价是：这个框架没有刹车；它解释了野心，却没告诉你如何阻止它践踏他人。

quote.en: the struggle, be it great or small, turns everywhere on predominance, on increase and expansion, on power, in conformity to the will to power, which is just the will to live.
quote.zh: the struggle, be it great or small, turns everywhere on predominance, on increase and expansion, on power, in conformity to the will to power, which is just the will to live.

label.en: Friedrich Nietzsche, The Joyful Wisdom (The Gay Science), §349, trans. Thomas Common
label.zh: 尼采《快乐的科学》第 349 节，科蒙 英译

claim.en: I argued that merely holding power tends to breed a love of it, and that the remedy is to spread power widely among the whole people.
claim.zh: 我论证过，仅仅握有权力，就容易滋生对权力的迷恋；对策是把权力广泛分散到全体人民之中。

detail.en: By this argument, a humble candidate becomes a different person after years in office, so character tests at the door matter less than limits once inside. The cost is that diffusing power also diffuses responsibility, and slows down decisions that sometimes need speed.
detail.zh: 照这个论证，一个谦逊的候选人在位多年后也会变成另一个人，所以门口的品格审查，不如进门后的权力限制重要。代价是：分散权力也分散了责任，并拖慢那些有时需要速度的决定。

quote.en: The mere possession of power tends to produce a love of power, which is a very dangerous motive, because the only sure proof of power consists in preventing others from doing what they wish to do. The essential theory of democracy is the diffusion of power among the whole people
quote.zh: The mere possession of power tends to produce a love of power, which is a very dangerous motive, because the only sure proof of power consists in preventing others from doing what they wish to do. The essential theory of democracy is the diffusion of power among the whole people

label.en: Bertrand Russell, Political Ideals (1917), ch. I
label.zh: 罗素《政治理想》（1917）第一章

claim.en: I taught that coveting the high office needed to govern a people is wrong in itself, even when that office is filled well, and that a man who loves ruling more than doing good is no true bishop.
claim.zh: 我教导说，觊觎治理百姓所需的高位本身就是不当的，即使那个职位被人妥善担任；爱统治胜过爱行善的人，不是真正的主教。

detail.en: This is a rule about desire, not results: Augustine grants that the covetous may govern well and still calls the coveting wrong. Applying a passage about bishops to political office is ours. Plato's reluctance is a judgement about which city runs best, while Augustine's concerns the state of the person; the cost is that it disqualifies by motive, which no one can see.
detail.zh: 这是关于欲望的规则，而不是关于结果的：奥古斯丁承认觊觎者也可能治理得好，但仍说觊觎本身是错的。把一段谈主教的话用到政治职位上，是我们的引申。柏拉图的不情愿是对哪座城邦治理得最好的判断，奥古斯丁关注的则是人本身的状态；代价是，它以动机取消资格，而动机是谁也看不见的。

quote.en: So that he who loves to govern rather than to do good is no bishop. Accordingly no one is prohibited from the search after truth, for in this leisure may most laudably be spent; but it is unseemly to covet the high position requisite for governing the people, even though that position be held and that government be administered in a seemly manner.
quote.zh: So that he who loves to govern rather than to do good is no bishop. Accordingly no one is prohibited from the search after truth, for in this leisure may most laudably be spent; but it is unseemly to covet the high position requisite for governing the people, even though that position be held and that government be administered in a seemly manner.

label.en: Augustine, The City of God, Book XIX, ch. 19, trans. Marcus Dods
label.zh: 奥古斯丁《上帝之城》第十九卷第十九章，多兹 英译

claim.en: I held that a restless desire for ever more power is common to all mankind and ends only in death, and that it comes less from greed than from insecurity: no one can secure what they have without acquiring more.
claim.zh: 我认为，对越来越多权力永不停息的欲望是全人类共有的，至死方休；它与其说出于贪婪，不如说出于不安：人若不获取更多，就保不住已有的东西。

detail.en: Hobbes is describing human nature, not praising it, and he built a whole state to restrain this desire. If he is right, disqualifying the ambitious disqualifies everyone, so the question becomes how power is checked rather than who wants it; that application is ours. Critics have called his picture a portrait of his own violent century rather than of humanity.
detail.zh: 霍布斯是在描述人性，而不是赞美它，他构建整个国家正是为了约束这种欲望。如果他是对的，取消有野心者的资格就等于取消所有人的资格，于是问题变成如何制约权力，而不是谁想要它；这一引申是我们的。批评者认为，他画的是自己那个暴烈的世纪，而不是人性本身。

quote.en: So that in the first place, I put for a general inclination of all mankind, a perpetual and restless desire of power after power, that ceaseth only in death. And the cause of this, is not always that a man hopes for a more intensive delight, than he has already attained to; or that he cannot be content with a moderate power: but because he cannot assure the power and means to live well, which he hath present, without the acquisition of more.
quote.zh: So that in the first place, I put for a general inclination of all mankind, a perpetual and restless desire of power after power, that ceaseth only in death. And the cause of this, is not always that a man hopes for a more intensive delight, than he has already attained to; or that he cannot be content with a moderate power: but because he cannot assure the power and means to live well, which he hath present, without the acquisition of more.

label.en: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, ch. XI, in The English Works, vol. III, ed. William Molesworth
label.zh: 霍布斯《利维坦》第十一章，收入莫尔斯沃思编《英文著作集》第三卷

claim.en: I held that seeking power is lawful when its aim is the power to do good, and that the danger lies in office itself, which opens the way to evil as well as good.
claim.zh: 我认为，追求权力，如果目的是获得行善的力量，便是正当的；危险在于职位本身，它既为行善也为作恶打开了门。

detail.en: Bacon adds the old saying that a place shows the man, some for the better and some for the worse, and he was later impeached for taking bribes as Lord Chancellor. Reading the essay as an answer to whether ambition should disqualify is ours. Its weakness is that doing good is the reason every aspirant gives.
detail.zh: 培根还引用一句古话：位置显出人的本相，有人变得更好，有人变得更坏；而他自己后来身为大法官，因受贿被弹劾。把这篇随笔读作对野心是否应取消资格的回答，是我们的引申。弱点是，为了行善是每个追求者都会给出的理由。

quote.en: In place, there is license to do good, and evil; whereof the latter is a curse: for in evil, the best condition is not to win; the second, not to can. But power to do good, is the true and lawful end of aspiring.
quote.zh: In place, there is license to do good, and evil; whereof the latter is a curse: for in evil, the best condition is not to win; the second, not to can. But power to do good, is the true and lawful end of aspiring.

label.en: Francis Bacon, Essays, "Of Great Place"
label.zh: 弗朗西斯·培根《随笔集》〈论高位〉

claim.en: I held that competition pushes sellers to serve buyers, and I expected people of the same trade to conspire against the public whenever they could. On my account, being better wins only while rivals are still free to undersell.
claim.zh: 我认为竞争迫使卖家为买家服务，也预料同行一有机会就会合谋损害公众。在我看来，只有对手还能自由压价时，更好的才能胜出。

detail.en: So the honest answer is conditional: better products win in open markets, and winners then try to close them. The cost is that the same passage warns the law can't simply ban such meetings, leaving no clean remedy.
detail.zh: 所以诚实的回答是有条件的：在开放市场中更好的产品会赢，而赢家随后会试图关闭市场。代价是：同一段话还警告说，法律无法简单地禁止这类聚会，因此并没有干净利落的补救办法。

quote.en: People of the same trade seldom meet together, even for merriment and diversion, but the conversation ends in a conspiracy against the public, or in some contrivance to raise prices.
quote.zh: People of the same trade seldom meet together, even for merriment and diversion, but the conversation ends in a conspiracy against the public, or in some contrivance to raise prices.

label.en: Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations, Book I, ch. X, part II
label.zh: 亚当·斯密《国富论》第一卷第十章第二节

claim.en: I argued that free competition makes the logic of capital bear on every single capitalist as a compulsion from outside: the owner who will not squeeze harder is undersold by one who will. Ruthlessness, on my account, is not a temperament but a law the market imposes.
claim.zh: 我论证过，自由竞争让资本的逻辑作为一种外部强制，压在每一个资本家身上：不肯压榨得更狠的老板，会被肯这样做的人挤垮。在我看来，冷酷不是一种性格，而是市场强加的法则。

detail.en: This shifts blame from individual executives to the structure, which is the argument's strength and its weakness. The cost: if competition compels everything, it is hard to explain firms in the same market that behave very differently.
detail.zh: 这把责任从个别高管转移到了结构上，这既是论证的长处，也是它的弱点。代价是：如果竞争决定一切，就很难解释同一市场中行为迥异的企业。

quote.en: Free competition brings out the inherent laws of capitalist production, in the shape of external coercive laws having power over every individual capitalist.
quote.zh: Free competition brings out the inherent laws of capitalist production, in the shape of external coercive laws having power over every individual capitalist.

label.en: Karl Marx, Capital, vol. I, ch. X, trans. Samuel Moore and Edward Aveling
label.zh: 马克思《资本论》第一卷第十章，穆尔与艾威林 英译

claim.en: I held that exploitation is not the mark of a corrupt or primitive society but belongs to the nature of living things, since to live is at bottom to take, to injure and to overpower the weaker.
claim.zh: 我认为，剥削不是腐败或原始社会的标志，而属于生命体的本性，因为活着从根本上就是夺取、伤害和征服较弱者。

detail.en: Nietzsche was writing about life and culture, not commerce; the application to companies is ours. The cost is plain: it is a description that can be used as permission. (Capitals mark emphasis in this translation.)
detail.zh: 尼采谈的是生命与文化，不是商业；把它用于公司是我们的推论。代价很明显：这是一种可以被当作许可来用的描述。（大写字母是该译本表示强调的方式。）

quote.en: life itself is ESSENTIALLY appropriation, injury, conquest of the strange and weak, suppression, severity, obtrusion of peculiar forms, incorporation, and at the least, putting it mildest, exploitation
quote.zh: life itself is ESSENTIALLY appropriation, injury, conquest of the strange and weak, suppression, severity, obtrusion of peculiar forms, incorporation, and at the least, putting it mildest, exploitation

label.en: Friedrich Nietzsche, Beyond Good and Evil, §259, trans. Helen Zimmern
label.zh: 尼采《善恶的彼岸》第 259 节，齐默恩 英译

claim.en: I read the record of nature as favouring the species that cooperate, not those that fight hardest, and I argued against using Darwin to justify cutthroat competition.
claim.zh: 我从自然的记录中读出，受青睐的是互相合作的物种，而不是斗得最凶的物种；我反对借达尔文为你死我活的竞争辩护。

detail.en: The extension to markets is our inference; Kropotkin was arguing against the use of Darwin to justify cutthroat competition. The cost is that in the short run the ruthless often do win, and 'the ones that last' can be a long wait.
detail.zh: 延伸到市场是我们的推论；克鲁泡特金当时是在反驳用达尔文来为残酷竞争辩护。代价是：在短期内狠的一方往往确实会赢，而「长久的赢家」可能要等很久。

quote.en: "Don't compete!--competition is always injurious to the species, and you have plenty of resources to avoid it!"
quote.zh: "Don't compete!--competition is always injurious to the species, and you have plenty of resources to avoid it!"

label.en: Peter Kropotkin, Mutual Aid, ch. II
label.zh: 克鲁泡特金《互助论》第二章

claim.en: I granted that whoever wins a contest gains from the losers' wasted effort and disappointment, and held that society should still let people compete. It should step in only when success is won by fraud, treachery or force.
claim.zh: 我承认，竞争中的赢家都从输家白费的努力与失望中获益，但我认为社会仍应让人们去竞争；只有当成功靠欺诈、背信或暴力得来时，社会才应介入。

detail.en: Carried to business, this is our reading: winning by being better is legitimate, winning by fraud is not, and the line between them is the whole question. Mill wrote about individuals in professions and examinations, not firms with market power. The weakness is that he leaves lawful but ruthless tactics, like pricing a smaller rival out of business, on the permitted side.
detail.zh: 把它用到企业上是我们的读法：靠更好取胜是正当的，靠欺诈取胜则不是，而两者的界线正是问题所在。密尔写的是职业和考试中的个人，而不是握有市场力量的公司。弱点在于：像用低价把小对手挤垮这类合法却狠辣的手段，在他的标准下仍属允许之列。

quote.en: Whoever succeeds in an overcrowded profession, or in a competitive examination; whoever is preferred to another in any contest for an object which both desire, reaps benefit from the loss of others, from their wasted exertion and their disappointment. But it is, by common admission, better for the general interest of mankind, that persons should pursue their objects undeterred by this sort of consequences. In other words, society admits no rights, either legal or moral, in the disappointed competitors, to immunity from this kind of suffering; and feels called on to interfere, only when means of success have been employed which it is contrary to the general interest to permit--namely, fraud or treachery, and force.
quote.zh: Whoever succeeds in an overcrowded profession, or in a competitive examination; whoever is preferred to another in any contest for an object which both desire, reaps benefit from the loss of others, from their wasted exertion and their disappointment. But it is, by common admission, better for the general interest of mankind, that persons should pursue their objects undeterred by this sort of consequences. In other words, society admits no rights, either legal or moral, in the disappointed competitors, to immunity from this kind of suffering; and feels called on to interfere, only when means of success have been employed which it is contrary to the general interest to permit--namely, fraud or treachery, and force.

label.en: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty, ch. V
label.zh: 约翰·斯图亚特·密尔《论自由》第五章

claim.en: I named competition first among the three natural causes of quarrel: where no common power keeps people in awe, they invade one another for gain. Ruthlessness, on my account, is what ordinary people do when nothing stops them.
claim.zh: 我把竞争列为人类争斗的三大自然原因之首：在没有共同权力使众人慑服的地方，人们会为了利益相互侵犯。在我看来，残酷不过是普通人在无人阻拦时会做的事。

detail.en: Hobbes was describing life without a state, not a market; reading a market with weak enforcement as a small version of it is our application. Unlike Marx, he blames human nature plus a missing referee rather than capitalism itself. The cost is that his remedy is a strong sovereign, and a powerful regulator can be captured by the very winners it is meant to restrain.
detail.zh: 霍布斯描述的是没有国家的生活，而不是市场；把执法薄弱的市场看作它的缩影，是我们的引申。与马克思不同，他归咎的是人性加上裁判缺席，而不是资本主义本身。代价是：他的解药是强大的主权者，而强有力的监管者也可能被它本该约束的赢家所俘获。

quote.en: So that in the nature of man, we find three principal causes of quarrel. First, competition; secondly, diffidence; thirdly, glory.
quote.zh: So that in the nature of man, we find three principal causes of quarrel. First, competition; secondly, diffidence; thirdly, glory.

label.en: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, ch. XIII, in The English Works, vol. III, ed. William Molesworth
label.zh: 霍布斯《利维坦》第十三章，收于莫尔斯沃思编《霍布斯英文著作集》第三卷

claim.en: I held that people are selfish and seldom grateful, yet learn to serve strangers without any real kindness, because each expects the service returned. Trust, on my account, is a convention that self-interest builds and keeps.
claim.zh: 我认为人自私、少有感恩之心，却能学会在毫无真正善意的情况下为陌生人效劳，因为每个人都预期对方会回报。在我看来，信任是由自利建立并维持的惯例。

detail.en: Applied to business, this is our reading: the firms that last are the ones others can count on, and that reliability is itself the edge. Unlike Kropotkin, Hume needs no goodwill, only long memories and repeated dealings. The weakness is that the convention holds only where dealings repeat; a firm that expects one big score has little reason to keep faith.
detail.zh: 用到商业上是我们的读法：能长久的公司，是别人可以指望的公司，而这种可靠本身就是优势。与克鲁泡特金不同，休谟不需要善意，只需要长久的记忆和反复的往来。弱点在于：这种惯例只在往来反复时才成立；一家只想赚一大笔就走的公司，几乎没有理由守信。

quote.en: Hence I learn to do a service to another, without bearing him any real kindness; because I forsee, that he will return my service, in expectation of another of the same kind, and in order to maintain the same correspondence of good offices with me or with others.
quote.zh: Hence I learn to do a service to another, without bearing him any real kindness; because I forsee, that he will return my service, in expectation of another of the same kind, and in order to maintain the same correspondence of good offices with me or with others.

label.en: David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book III, Part II, §V
label.zh: 大卫·休谟《人性论》第三卷第二部分第五节

claim.en: Through Socrates in the Republic I argued that if anyone may lie, it should be the rulers, for the public good, and that a private citizen who lies to them commits a graver fault.
claim.zh: 我在《理想国》中借苏格拉底之口论证：如果有谁可以说谎，那应当是统治者，而且只为公共利益；普通公民对统治者说谎，则是更重的过错。

detail.en: This is the origin of the 'noble lie' debate. The cost is obvious and old: it hands the decision about what counts as the public good to the people doing the lying.
detail.zh: 这正是「高贵的谎言」之争的源头。代价显而易见且古老：它把「什么算公共利益」的决定权，交给了说谎的人自己。

quote.en: Then if any one at all is to have the privilege of lying, the rulers of the State should be the persons; and they, in their dealings either with enemies or with their own citizens, may be allowed to lie for the public good.
quote.zh: Then if any one at all is to have the privilege of lying, the rulers of the State should be the persons; and they, in their dealings either with enemies or with their own citizens, may be allowed to lie for the public good.

label.en: Plato, Republic, Book III (389b), trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 柏拉图《理想国》第三卷（389b），乔伊特 英译

claim.en: I argued that a wise prince cannot keep faith when doing so would be turned against him, because men are not good and will not keep faith with him. If men were all good, I said, the rule would not hold.
claim.zh: 我论证过，当守信会被用来对付自己时，明智的君主不能守信，因为人并不善良，也不会对他守信。我说过，如果人人都善良，这条规则就不成立。

detail.en: He adds, tellingly, that if men were good the rule would not hold. The cost is that the argument works equally well for a ruler protecting himself, and Machiavelli does not much distinguish the two.
detail.zh: 他还意味深长地补充说，如果人都是好的，这条规则就不成立。代价是：这个论证同样适用于一个保护自己的统治者，而马基雅维利并没有认真区分二者。

quote.en: Therefore a wise lord cannot, nor ought he to, keep faith when such observance may be turned against him, and when the reasons that caused him to pledge it exist no longer. If men were entirely good this precept would not hold, but because they are bad, and will not keep faith with you, you too are not bound to observe it with them.
quote.zh: Therefore a wise lord cannot, nor ought he to, keep faith when such observance may be turned against him, and when the reasons that caused him to pledge it exist no longer. If men were entirely good this precept would not hold, but because they are bad, and will not keep faith with you, you too are not bound to observe it with them.

label.en: Niccolò Machiavelli, The Prince, ch. XVIII, trans. W. K. Marriott
label.zh: 马基雅维利《君主论》第十八章，马里奥特 英译

claim.en: I argued that a lying promise uses the other person merely as a means, someone who cannot share in the end being pursued. I allowed no exception to truthfulness, not even for a murderer at the door.
claim.zh: 我论证过，虚假的承诺把对方仅仅当作手段，对方无法分享所追求的目的。我不允许说真话的义务有任何例外，即使面对门口的凶手也是如此。

detail.en: The extension to state lies is ours, though Kant elsewhere refused even a lie to a murderer at the door. The cost is that this rigour leaves officials no room in situations where silence is impossible and truth would cost lives.
detail.zh: 延伸到国家谎言是我们的推论，尽管康德在别处连对门口的凶手说谎都不允许。代价是：这种严格，让官员在无法沉默、说真话又会害死人的处境中毫无余地。

quote.en: He who is thinking of making a lying promise to others will see at once that he would be using another man merely as a mean, without the latter containing at the same time the end in himself.
quote.zh: He who is thinking of making a lying promise to others will see at once that he would be using another man merely as a mean, without the latter containing at the same time the end in himself.

label.en: Immanuel Kant, Groundwork of the Metaphysic of Morals, Second Section, trans. T. K. Abbott
label.zh: 康德《道德形而上学奠基》第二章，阿博特 英译

claim.en: I taught that every lie is a sin, though intention and subject matter make a great difference to how grave it is: a lie told to help is less grave than one told to harm.
claim.zh: 我教导说，每一个谎言都是罪，但意图和所涉之事会极大地影响它的轻重：为帮助人而说的谎，比为伤害人而说的谎轻。

detail.en: This is a religious teaching about sin, not a theory of statecraft. The cost is that it gives a government no permission at all — useful as a check, hard to live by in a war.
detail.zh: 这是一条关于罪的宗教教导，而不是治国理论。代价是：它没有给政府任何许可——作为制约很有用，在战争中却很难践行。

quote.en: To me, however, it seems certain that every lie is a sin, though it makes a great difference with what intention and on what subject one lies.
quote.zh: To me, however, it seems certain that every lie is a sin, though it makes a great difference with what intention and on what subject one lies.

label.en: Augustine, Enchiridion, ch. 18, trans. J. F. Shaw
label.zh: 奥古斯丁《教义手册》第十八章，肖 英译

claim.en: I granted that the public good may require men to betray and to lie, but I wanted no part of that work. I left the commission to more pliant men.
claim.zh: 我承认公共利益也许需要人去背叛、去说谎，但我不想参与这种事。我把这份差事留给那些更顺从、更圆滑的人。

detail.en: He does not pretend the lie becomes honest because it serves the state; he calls it a vice the state happens to need. The cost is that stepping aside leaves the dirty work to whoever is willing, which is not obviously better.
detail.zh: 他并不假装谎言因为服务国家就变得正当；他称之为国家恰好需要的恶。代价是：袖手旁观，等于把脏活留给愿意干的人，而这显然未必更好。

quote.en: The public weal requires that men should betray, and lie, and massacre; let us leave this commission to men who are more obedient and more supple.
quote.zh: The public weal requires that men should betray, and lie, and massacre; let us leave this commission to men who are more obedient and more supple.

label.en: Michel de Montaigne, Essays, Book III, ch. 1 "Of Profit and Honesty", trans. Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt
label.zh: 蒙田《随笔集》第三卷第一章〈论利与义〉，科顿 英译，黑兹利特 编

claim.en: I argued that the obligation of justice between states is weaker than between individuals, so a prince or minister who deceives another state deserves more indulgence than a private gentleman who breaks his word.
claim.zh: 我论证过，国与国之间的正义义务弱于人与人之间，因此欺骗他国的君主或大臣，比食言的普通绅士更应得到宽容。

detail.en: Hume is talking about treaties between rulers, not lies a government tells its own citizens; stretching it that far is our step. The cost is that his scale is one of degree with no floor, so it offers no point at which a state's deception stops being excusable.
detail.zh: 休谟谈的是统治者之间的条约，而不是政府对本国公民说的谎；把它延伸到那里是我们的推论。代价是：他的尺度只讲程度、没有底线，因此没有给出国家的欺骗在哪一点上不再可以原谅。

quote.en: Since, therefore, the natural obligation to justice, among different states, is not so strong as among individuals, the moral obligation, which arises from it, must partake of its weakness; and we must necessarily give a greater indulgence to a prince or minister, who deceives another; than to a private gentleman, who breaks his word of honour.
quote.zh: Since, therefore, the natural obligation to justice, among different states, is not so strong as among individuals, the moral obligation, which arises from it, must partake of its weakness; and we must necessarily give a greater indulgence to a prince or minister, who deceives another; than to a private gentleman, who breaks his word of honour.

label.en: David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book III, Part II, §XI
label.zh: 大卫·休谟《人性论》第三卷第二部分第十一节

claim.en: I held that where there is no common power there is no law, and so no injustice; in war, force and fraud are the cardinal virtues. Sovereigns, I argued, stand toward one another in that posture.
claim.zh: 我认为，没有共同权力的地方就没有法律，因而也无所谓不义；在战争中，暴力与欺诈是两大美德。我论证过，主权者彼此之间正处于这种态势。

detail.en: On this view a state that keeps faith with rivals who do not is disarming itself; that is our application of his account of war to diplomacy. The cost is that it says nothing about lies told inside a state, where Hobbes thinks law does hold, and that the same logic excuses every rival's deceit too.
detail.zh: 照此看法，一个国家对不守信的对手守信，等于自缴武器；把他对战争状态的描述用到外交上，是我们的引申。代价是：它对国家内部说的谎只字未提，而霍布斯认为在国内法律确实有效；而且同样的逻辑也替每一个对手的欺骗开脱。

quote.en: Where there is no common power, there is no law: where no law, no injustice. Force, and fraud, are in war the two cardinal virtues.
quote.zh: Where there is no common power, there is no law: where no law, no injustice. Force, and fraud, are in war the two cardinal virtues.

label.en: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, ch. XIII
label.zh: 霍布斯《利维坦》第十三章

claim.en: I held that keeping secrets and dissembling are often necessary, but that simulation, outright false profession, is more culpable and less politic, allowable only in great and rare matters.
claim.zh: 我认为，保守秘密和掩饰常常是必要的，但伪装，也就是公然的虚假表白，更应受责备，也更不明智，只有在重大而罕见的事情上才可允许。

detail.en: Bacon wrote for courtiers and statesmen, so the 'great and rare matters' plausibly include affairs of state, though the essay does not name them; applying it to national lies is ours. He also warned that the habit costs the liar trust, which is the stain in practical form. The weakness is that he gives no test for what counts as great and rare.
detail.zh: 培根是写给廷臣和政治家看的，所以重大而罕见的事情很可能包括国事，但文中并未点明；把它用到为国说谎上是我们的推论。他也提醒，这种习惯会让说谎者失去信任，这就是污点的实际形态。弱点是：他没有给出判断何为重大而罕见的标准。

quote.en: But for the third degree, which is simulation, and false profession; that I hold more culpable, and less politic; except it be in great and rare matters.
quote.zh: But for the third degree, which is simulation, and false profession; that I hold more culpable, and less politic; except it be in great and rare matters.

label.en: Francis Bacon, Essays, "Of Simulation and Dissimulation"
label.zh: 培根《随笔集》〈论伪装与掩饰〉

claim.en: Through Socrates I argued that steering the ship of state takes a navigator's knowledge, and that a true ruler does not plead with the people for the right to rule them.
claim.zh: 我借苏格拉底之口论证：驾驶国家之船需要舵手的知识，而真正的统治者不会恳求民众让他来统治。

detail.en: The cost is the one critics have pressed for two thousand years: who certifies the expert, and what stops expertise from serving itself? Plato's answer was a philosopher class with no private property — a price no modern state has paid.
detail.zh: 代价正是两千年来批评者一再追问的：谁来认证专家？又有什么能阻止专长为自己服务？柏拉图的回答是一个没有私产的哲人阶层——没有哪个现代国家付出过这样的代价。

quote.en: The ruler who is good for anything ought not to beg his subjects to be ruled by him
quote.zh: The ruler who is good for anything ought not to beg his subjects to be ruled by him

label.en: Plato, Republic, Book VI (489b–c), trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 柏拉图《理想国》第六卷（489b–c），乔伊特 英译

claim.en: I held that when two judgements differ, the wiser has a claim to more weight in common affairs, and I admitted that the difficulty lies in telling which one is wiser.
claim.zh: 我认为，当两种判断相左时，更明智的那一种在共同事务中应当占更大分量；我也承认，难点在于确定哪一种更明智。

detail.en: Mill's own remedy was extra votes for the educated, an idea later democrats rejected. The cost is visible in the quote itself: a leader 'better than you' needs some test of betterness, and every test so far has favoured those who wrote it.
detail.zh: 密尔自己的方案是给受过教育者更多选票，这个主张后来被民主派抛弃了。代价就写在引文里：「比你更好」的领导需要某种衡量「更好」的标准，而迄今每一种标准都偏向制定它的人。

quote.en: One of the two, as the wiser or better man, has a claim to superior weight: the difficulty is in ascertaining which of the two it is
quote.zh: One of the two, as the wiser or better man, has a claim to superior weight: the difficulty is in ascertaining which of the two it is

label.en: John Stuart Mill, Considerations on Representative Government, ch. VIII
label.zh: 约翰·斯图亚特·密尔《代议制政府》第八章

claim.en: I argued that the many, judging together, judge many things better than any single person, however able, as a feast to which many contribute is better than one man's portion.
claim.zh: 我论证过，众人一起判断，在许多事情上胜过任何一个人，无论他多能干，正如众人合办的宴席胜过一个人的一份饭。

detail.en: This argues for leaders who stay close to the people and answerable to them, not for leaders who are average. The cost is that Aristotle limited 'the people' to free male citizens, and the argument works only when the many actually deliberate together rather than simply vote apart.
detail.zh: 这论证的是领导者应贴近民众、向民众负责，而不是领导者应当平庸。代价是：亚里士多德所说的「民众」只包括自由的男性公民，而且这个论证只有在多数人真正一起商议、而不是各自投票时才成立。

quote.en: one individual, be he who he will, will be found, upon comparison, inferior to a whole people taken collectively: but this is what a city is, as a public entertainment is better than one man's portion: for this reason the multitude judge of many things better than any one single person.
quote.zh: one individual, be he who he will, will be found, upon comparison, inferior to a whole people taken collectively: but this is what a city is, as a public entertainment is better than one man's portion: for this reason the multitude judge of many things better than any one single person.

label.en: Aristotle, Politics, Book III, ch. 15, trans. William Ellis
label.zh: 亚里士多德《政治学》第三卷第十五章，埃利斯 英译

claim.en: I held that sovereignty is the exercise of the general will and can never be handed over. A ruler may be given power, but no one can carry the people's will for them.
claim.zh: 我认为，主权就是公意的运用，永远不能转让。统治者可以被赋予权力，但没有人能代替人民承担他们的意志。

detail.en: On this reading, the right leader is a servant carrying out what the people decided, whether wiser than you or not. The cost is that Rousseau's model fits a small republic where citizens can assemble; scaled to a large country, it is hard to say who speaks for the general will.
detail.zh: 照这个读法，合适的领导者是执行人民决定的仆人，无论他比你聪明与否。代价是：卢梭的模式适合公民能够集会的小共和国；放大到一个大国，很难说谁在为公意发声。

quote.en: I hold then that Sovereignty, being nothing less than the exercise of the general will, can never be alienated, and that the Sovereign, who is no less than a collective being, cannot be represented except by himself: the power indeed may be transmitted, but not the will.
quote.zh: I hold then that Sovereignty, being nothing less than the exercise of the general will, can never be alienated, and that the Sovereign, who is no less than a collective being, cannot be represented except by himself: the power indeed may be transmitted, but not the will.

label.en: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, The Social Contract, Book II, ch. 1, trans. G. D. H. Cole
label.zh: 卢梭《社会契约论》第二卷第一章，柯尔 英译

claim.en: I counted it a real loss when a group's leader was effectively chosen for it from outside, because a group learns by searching for, criticising and commissioning its own leaders.
claim.zh: 我认为，当一个群体的领袖实际上由外人替它选定时，这是真正的损失，因为一个群体正是在寻找、批评并委任自己的领袖时受到教育。

detail.en: By this measure the question is less 'like you or better' than 'whose choice'. A leader can be more gifted than the people they lead and still be theirs, if they rose from them and answer to them. The cost is that search and criticism take time and conflict, and Du Bois wrote this in open disagreement with the most powerful Black leader of his day.
detail.zh: 照这个标准，问题与其说是「像你还是比你强」，不如说是「由谁来选」。一个领导者可以比他所领导的人更有天赋，只要他从这些人中产生并对他们负责，他仍属于他们。代价是：寻找与批评需要时间，也会带来冲突，而杜波依斯写下这段话时，正与当时最有权势的黑人领袖公开争论。

quote.en: a loss of that peculiarly valuable education which a group receives when by search and criticism it finds and commissions its own leaders.
quote.zh: a loss of that peculiarly valuable education which a group receives when by search and criticism it finds and commissions its own leaders.

label.en: W. E. B. Du Bois, The Souls of Black Folk, ch. III
label.zh: 杜波依斯《黑人的灵魂》第三章

claim.en: I held that the common people and the truly wise both judge well, and that the trouble comes from the half-learned between them, who think themselves wise and despise the rest.
claim.zh: 我认为，普通人和真正的智者都判断得当，麻烦出在两者之间那些一知半解的人：他们自以为聪明，看不起其他所有人。

detail.en: Pascal is not praising popular opinion without reserve: elsewhere he says the people's opinions are sound but held for the wrong reasons. Applying this to elections is ours. It cuts against the case for a leader better than you, since those most eager to lead because they know better may be exactly the half-learned he distrusts; its weakness is that it gives no way to tell the wise from the merely confident.
detail.zh: 帕斯卡并非无条件地赞美民意：他在别处说，百姓的看法是对的，但他们持有这些看法的理由是错的。把这段话用到选举上，是我们的引申。它对领导者应当比你更强这一主张构成反驳：那些因为自认懂得更多而最想领导的人，也许正是他所不信任的半通之人；它的弱点是，没有给出区分真正的智者和单纯自信者的办法。

quote.en: Those between the two, who have left their natural ignorance and not been able to reach the other, have some tincture of this vain knowledge, and assume to be wise. These trouble the world, and judge all things falsely. The people and the wise make up the world; these despise it, and are despised; they judge ill of all things, and the world rightly judges of them.
quote.zh: Those between the two, who have left their natural ignorance and not been able to reach the other, have some tincture of this vain knowledge, and assume to be wise. These trouble the world, and judge all things falsely. The people and the wise make up the world; these despise it, and are despised; they judge ill of all things, and the world rightly judges of them.

label.en: Blaise Pascal, Thoughts (Pensées), trans. C. Kegan Paul
label.zh: 帕斯卡《思想录》，凯根·保罗 英译

claim.en: I argued that the people are the authors of what their representative does in their name, and that when they limit his commission, they own no more of his acts than they authorised.
claim.zh: 我论证过，人民是其代表者以他们名义所做之事的作者；而当他们限定了委托的范围，他们所承担的就不超过他们所授权的部分。

detail.en: Hobbes meant this to strengthen the sovereign: give authority without limit and you own everything the ruler does, including what you hate. Reading it as a case for leaders who carry out the people's will is ours, and it cuts both ways. The useful point is the last clause: authority given with limits binds you only so far.
detail.zh: 霍布斯的本意是加强主权者：无限制地授权，你就要承认统治者的一切作为都是你的，包括你厌恶的那些。把它读成领导者应执行人民意志的理由，是我们的引申，而且这把刀两面都割。有用的是最后一句：有限度的授权，只在那个限度内约束你。

quote.en: they cannot be understood for one; but many authors, of every thing their representative saith, or doth in their name; every man giving their common representer, authority from himself in particular; and owning all the actions the representer doth, in case they give him authority without stint: otherwise, when they limit him in what, and how far he shall represent them, none of them owneth more than they gave him commission to act.
quote.zh: they cannot be understood for one; but many authors, of every thing their representative saith, or doth in their name; every man giving their common representer, authority from himself in particular; and owning all the actions the representer doth, in case they give him authority without stint: otherwise, when they limit him in what, and how far he shall represent them, none of them owneth more than they gave him commission to act.

label.en: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, ch. XVI, in The English Works, vol. III, ed. William Molesworth
label.zh: 霍布斯《利维坦》第十六章，收入莫尔斯沃思编《英文著作集》第三卷

claim.en: I argued that democracy stays a social reality only if leaders and led keep common ground in their experience. In the Chicago wards I knew, voters chose the alderman who lived as they did.
claim.zh: 我论证过，只有领导者和被领导者在经验上保持共同的基础，民主才是一种真实的社会表达。在我熟悉的芝加哥选区里，选民选出的是和他们过着同样生活的市议员。

detail.en: Addams was not defending that alderman: she shows him corrupt and still re-elected, because his standard suited his constituents. Turning her observation into an answer about national leaders is ours. Her point is that shared experience earns trust, and trust can cover a great deal; the cost is that one of you may also share your failings.
detail.zh: 亚当斯并不是在为那位市议员辩护：她写出他腐败却仍然连任，因为他的标准正合选民的口味。把她的观察变成对国家领导人问题的回答，是我们的引申。她的要点是，共同的经验赢得信任，而信任可以遮掩很多东西；代价是，你们中的一员也可能带着你们的缺点。

quote.en: It is most difficult to hold to our political democracy and to make it in any sense a social expression and not a mere governmental contrivance, unless we take pains to keep on common ground in our human experiences. Otherwise there is in various parts of the community an inevitable difference of ethical standards which becomes responsible for much misunderstanding.
quote.zh: It is most difficult to hold to our political democracy and to make it in any sense a social expression and not a mere governmental contrivance, unless we take pains to keep on common ground in our human experiences. Otherwise there is in various parts of the community an inevitable difference of ethical standards which becomes responsible for much misunderstanding.

label.en: Jane Addams, Democracy and Social Ethics
label.zh: 简·亚当斯《民主与社会伦理》

claim.en: I argued that production exists for the sake of the consumer, and that the producer's interest deserves attention only as far as it serves the buyer's. I wrote this against merchants who rigged the rules of trade for themselves.
claim.zh: 我论证过，生产是为了消费者而存在的，生产者的利益只有在服务于买家的利益时才值得照顾。我写这些，是针对那些为自己操纵贸易规则的商人。

detail.en: Smith wrote this against merchants who rigged trade rules for themselves, so the claim is about whose interest counts, not a proof that the winner is best. The cost: buyers choose under limited information and switching costs, which Smith's sentence does not address.
detail.zh: 斯密写这句话，是为了反对那些为自己操纵贸易规则的商人，所以它讲的是谁的利益应被优先，而不是证明赢家最好。代价是：买家是在信息有限、转换成本存在的情况下做选择的，而斯密这句话并未处理这一点。

quote.en: Consumption is the sole end and purpose of all production; and the interest of the producer ought to be attended to, only so far as it may be necessary for promoting that of the consumer.
quote.zh: Consumption is the sole end and purpose of all production; and the interest of the producer ought to be attended to, only so far as it may be necessary for promoting that of the consumer.

label.en: Adam Smith, The Wealth of Nations, Book IV, ch. VIII
label.zh: 亚当·斯密《国富论》第四卷第八章

claim.en: I held that the more desirable of two pleasures is the one preferred by people who have experienced both. My test counts the verdict of those who know both options, not of everyone.
claim.zh: 我认为，两种快乐之中，更值得追求的是那些两者都体验过的人所偏爱的那一种。我的标准看重的是熟悉两者的人的判断，而不是所有人的判断。

detail.en: Mill was writing about pleasures, not products; the extension is ours. The cost is that 'competent judges' can become a polite word for snobs, and Mill gives no easy way to tell an expert from a taste-maker.
detail.zh: 密尔谈的是快乐，不是产品；延伸是我们的推论。代价是：「有资格的评判者」可能变成势利者的体面说法，而密尔没有给出简单的方法，来分辨专家和引领品味的人。

quote.en: Of two pleasures, if there be one to which all or almost all who have experience of both give a decided preference, irrespective of any feeling of moral obligation to prefer it, that is the more desirable pleasure.
quote.zh: Of two pleasures, if there be one to which all or almost all who have experience of both give a decided preference, irrespective of any feeling of moral obligation to prefer it, that is the more desirable pleasure.

label.en: John Stuart Mill, Utilitarianism, ch. II
label.zh: 约翰·斯图亚特·密尔《功利主义》第二章

claim.en: I cited a London inquiry into the bakers which found that the cheapest sellers' bread was adulterated with alum, chalk and stone-dust. I held that the market sees exchange value, not usefulness.
claim.zh: 我引用过伦敦对面包业的一项调查：那些低价出售者的面包里掺了明矾、白垩和石粉。我认为，市场看到的是交换价值，而不是使用价值。

detail.en: For Marx this is the general case: the market sees exchange value, not usefulness. The cost is that the example is from 1860s London before food-safety law; regulation and reputation now catch some of what the market alone missed, which complicates the general claim.
detail.zh: 在马克思看来，这是普遍情况：市场看见的是交换价值，而不是有用性。代价是：这个例子来自食品安全立法之前的 1860 年代伦敦；如今监管和声誉能捕捉到一部分单靠市场看不见的东西，这让他的普遍论断更复杂。

quote.en: The undersellers, almost without exception, sell bread adulterated with alum, soap, pearl ashes, chalk, Derbyshire stone-dust
quote.zh: The undersellers, almost without exception, sell bread adulterated with alum, soap, pearl ashes, chalk, Derbyshire stone-dust

label.en: Karl Marx, Capital, vol. I, ch. X, trans. Samuel Moore and Edward Aveling
label.zh: 马克思《资本论》第一卷第十章，穆尔与艾威林 英译

claim.en: I defined truth by what works in our thinking, but by what works over the long run and taken as a whole, not by what pays off at a single moment.
claim.zh: 我用在思考中行得通来定义真理，但要看长远、看整体，而不是看某一时刻是否划算。

detail.en: The extension from ideas to products is ours, though James himself used money metaphors freely. The cost is that 'the long run' never arrives on a date, so the pragmatist can always defer judgement.
detail.zh: 把它从观念延伸到产品是我们的推论，虽然詹姆斯本人常用金钱作比喻。代价是：「长远」永远不会在某个确定日期到来，所以实用主义者总可以推迟判断。

quote.en: 'The true,' to put it very briefly, is only the expedient in the way of our thinking, just as 'the right' is only the expedient in the way of our behaving. Expedient in almost any fashion; and expedient in the long run and on the whole of course
quote.zh: 'The true,' to put it very briefly, is only the expedient in the way of our thinking, just as 'the right' is only the expedient in the way of our behaving. Expedient in almost any fashion; and expedient in the long run and on the whole of course

label.en: William James, Pragmatism, Lecture VI
label.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯《实用主义》第六讲

claim.en: I argued that each person judges his own interest better than anyone else can, and that nobody freely agrees to what he believes will hurt him. I stated this as a rule of law about consent.
claim.zh: 我论证过，每个人对自身利益的判断都胜过别人，而且没有人会自愿同意他认为有害于自己的事。我把这当作关于同意的一条法律原则提出。

detail.en: Bentham stated this as a rule of law about consent, and reading sales figures as a verdict on quality is our extension. Where Smith makes the consumer the purpose of the economy, Bentham makes the consumer the judge. The weakness is in the wording: a buyer judges his own interest, not products he never tried, and Bentham himself allowed that people deceive themselves.
detail.zh: 边沁是把这当作关于「同意」的法律规则来讲的，把销量当作对品质的裁决，是我们的引申。斯密把消费者当作经济的目的，边沁则把消费者当作裁判。弱点就在措辞里：买家判断的是自身利益，而不是他从未试过的产品；边沁本人也承认人会自欺。

quote.en: This rule is founded upon two very simple propositions: one, that every person is the best judge of his own interest; the other, that no man will consent to what he thinks hurtful to himself.
quote.zh: This rule is founded upon two very simple propositions: one, that every person is the best judge of his own interest; the other, that no man will consent to what he thinks hurtful to himself.

label.en: Jeremy Bentham, The Theory of Legislation
label.zh: 边沁《立法理论》

claim.en: I wrote that popular praise follows show rather than substance: fame lifts up what is light and swollen and sinks what is weighty. The praise that lasts comes from people of judgment.
claim.zh: 我写过，大众的赞誉追随的是表面而非实质：名声把轻浮虚胀的东西托起，把厚重的东西沉没。能持久的赞誉，来自有判断力的人。

detail.en: Bacon was writing about praise of persons, and treating market share as a kind of fame is our reading. Where Mill asks those who know both options, Bacon asks those with judgment, which is harder to check. The cost is plain snobbery: it lets an expert dismiss what ordinary buyers really value as mere show.
detail.zh: 培根谈的是对人的赞誉，把市场份额当作一种名声，是我们的读法。密尔问的是两样都了解的人，培根问的是有判断力的人，后者更难核实。代价是明显的势利：它让专家可以把普通买家真正看重的东西斥为表面功夫。

quote.en: Certainly fame is like a river, that beareth up things light and swoln, and drowns things weighty and solid.
quote.zh: Certainly fame is like a river, that beareth up things light and swoln, and drowns things weighty and solid.

label.en: Francis Bacon, Essays, "Of Praise"
label.zh: 培根《随笔》〈论赞美〉

claim.en: I measured the cost of a thing by the amount of life that must be exchanged for it, now or in the long run. By that measure a price in dollars leaves out most of what a thing costs.
claim.zh: 我用必须为一样东西付出多少生命来衡量它的代价，无论眼下还是长远。照这个尺度，以美元计的价格漏掉了它大部分的代价。

detail.en: He was weighing a house against the years of labour it takes to pay for it, and turning this on market winners is our application. Unlike Marx's adulterated bread, Thoreau's point needs no fraud: an honest price can still misstate what a thing is worth to the person who pays it. The weakness is that life cannot be counted, so his test cannot rank two products the way a price can.
detail.zh: 他权衡的是一所房子与付清它所需的多年劳作，把这用到市场赢家上，是我们的引申。与马克思笔下掺假的面包不同，梭罗的观点不需要欺诈：一个诚实的价格，也可能错估一样东西对付钱的人究竟值多少。弱点在于：生命无法计数，所以他的检验不能像价格那样给两件产品排序。

quote.en: the cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.
quote.zh: the cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.

origin.zh: 马萨诸塞州康科德，1854 年

label.en: Henry David Thoreau, Walden, "Economy"
label.zh: 梭罗《瓦尔登湖》〈经济篇〉

claim.en: I argued that character is formed by practice: by doing just or brave acts again and again, a person becomes just or brave. What repeated activity produces is first of all the one who does it.
claim.zh: 我论证过，品格是由实践养成的：一再做公正或勇敢的事，人就成为公正或勇敢的人。反复的活动首先造就的，是做事的那个人。

detail.en: Years spent learning judgement, patience and precision therefore have not become meaningless because a machine can produce the final artefact faster. The cost is that this separates personal development from economic usefulness entirely: your expertise may genuinely have shaped you while becoming much less valuable in the labour market.
detail.zh: 因此，用来学习判断力、耐心与精确度的岁月，并不会因为机器能更快做出成品而失去意义。它的代价是把人的成长与经济价值彻底分开：你的专业也许真的塑造了你，同时在劳动市场上大幅贬值。

quote.en: We become just by doing just acts, temperate by doing temperate acts, brave by doing brave acts.
quote.zh: 我们因做公正的事而成为公正的人，因做节制的事而成为节制的人，因做勇敢的事而成为勇敢的人。

label.en: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, Book II, Chapter 1, trans. W. D. Ross
label.zh: 亚里士多德《尼各马可伦理学》第二卷第一章，罗斯 英译

claim.en: I held that life is a military school, and that the hardship a person comes through without being destroyed makes him stronger.
claim.zh: 我认为人生是一所军事学校，一个人熬过而没有被摧毁的艰难，会让他更强。

detail.en: Nietzsche would resist treating a decade of work as an investment whose worth can be read off a current price. The cost is that this can romanticise struggle: someone whose livelihood is disappearing may reasonably care far more about rent than about whether the training improved their character.
detail.zh: 尼采会反对把十年的努力当成一笔可以按当下价格清算的投资。它的代价是容易美化苦难：一个正在失去生计的人，完全有理由更关心房租，而不是这些训练是否让自己的品格变好。

quote.en: From the military school of life.—That which does not kill me, makes me stronger.
quote.zh: 出自人生的军事学校 — 那些杀不死我的，使我更强。

label.en: Friedrich Nietzsche, The Twilight of the Idols, "Maxims and Arrows" §8, trans. Anthony M. Ludovici
label.zh: 弗里德里希·尼采《偶像的黄昏》〈箴言与箭〉第 8 节，卢多维奇 英译

claim.en: I distinguished two kinds of work: one close to a blessing, carrying hope of rest, of a useful product and of pleasure in the doing; the other a mere burden on life, which I argued should be done away with.
claim.zh: 我区分过两种劳动：一种近乎祝福，带着休息的希望、有用产品的希望和做事本身的乐趣；另一种只是生命的负担，我主张应当把它废除。

detail.en: Morris held that worthwhile work carries hope of useful output, of rest, and of pleasure in the activity itself. If AI removes labour that has none of those, protecting it to keep people busy gets the problem backwards. The cost is that AI may remove work people do find meaningful alongside the work they hate — and someone has to decide which is which.
detail.zh: 莫里斯认为值得做的劳动包含三种希望：有用的产出、休息，以及活动本身的乐趣。如果 AI 拿走的正是三者皆无的劳动，为了让人有事可做而保护它，就把问题弄反了。代价是：AI 可能连人们真正觉得有意义的工作一起拿走，而由谁来判断哪些该留，仍然没有答案。

quote.en: Here, you see, are two kinds of work—one good, the other bad; one not far removed from a blessing, a lightening of life; the other a mere curse, a burden to life.
quote.zh: 你看，这里有两种劳动 — 一种好，一种坏；一种近乎祝福，让生命轻盈；另一种纯是诅咒，是生命的负担。

label.en: William Morris, Useful Work versus Useless Toil, 1884
label.zh: 威廉·莫里斯《有用的劳动与无用的苦役》，1884 年

claim.en: I predicted in 1930 that rising productivity would solve the economic problem within a century, and that the real task would become how to use the leisure it left. I treated that as a victory, not a catastrophe.
claim.zh: 我在1930年预言，生产率的提高将在一百年内解决经济问题，真正的难题会变成如何使用由此空出的闲暇。我把这看作胜利，而不是灾难。

detail.en: Keynes expected rising productivity to make much human labour unnecessary, and treated that as the victory rather than the catastrophe. His famous miss exposes the unresolved half: productivity can remove the need for someone's labour without giving that person any share of the abundance it creates.
detail.zh: 凯恩斯预期生产率上升终将让大量人类劳动变得不必要，并且把这看作胜利而非灾难。他这个著名的失准预测暴露了未解决的另一半：生产率可以取消对某个人劳动的需要，却不给这个人分配由此产生的富足。

quote.en: Three-hour shifts or a fifteen-hour week may put off the problem for a great while.
quote.zh: 三小时轮班，或者每周十五小时，也许能把这个问题推迟很久。

label.en: John Maynard Keynes, "Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren", 1930
label.zh: 约翰·梅纳德·凯恩斯〈我们后代的经济前景〉，1930 年

claim.en: I argued that the modern faith in work as a virtue does real harm, and that once production allowed it, a working day of four hours would leave room for leisure well used.
claim.zh: 我论证过，现代人把劳动奉为美德的信念造成了实实在在的伤害；一旦生产允许，每天工作四小时，就能为善用的闲暇留出空间。

detail.en: If society can produce what people need with far less labour, asking how humans stay equally busy may be the wrong question; the opening is leisure, curiosity, friendship and things done for their own sake. Russell concedes the difficulty himself: people who organised a whole life around work do not automatically know how to use time that is free.
detail.zh: 如果社会能用少得多的劳动生产出人们所需的东西，那么「如何让人继续一样忙」也许根本就是错的问题；真正的机会在于闲暇、好奇、友谊与那些为自身而做的事。罗素自己也承认困难：把整个人生围绕工作组织起来的人，并不会自动知道如何使用空出来的时间。

quote.en: A great deal of harm is being done in the modern world by belief in the virtuousness of work.
quote.zh: 现代世界正因为相信「劳动是美德」而造成大量伤害。

label.en: Bertrand Russell, "In Praise of Idleness", 1932
label.zh: 伯特兰·罗素〈闲散颂〉，1932 年

claim.en: I am the Preacher's book: I saw a man labour with all his heart and then leave everything to one who never laboured for it. I asked what all that toil had gained him, and found that achievement does not hold.
claim.zh: 我是传道者的书：我看见人用尽心力劳碌，却要把一切留给从未为此劳碌的人。我问这一切劳作给他带来了什么，发现成就留不住。

detail.en: You can become excellent, wealthy and admired and still lose control of everything you made. AI does not create that instability; it makes it visible far earlier in a career. The cost is that loosening identity from achievement says nothing about how to build a satisfying day once the work is gone.
detail.zh: 你可以变得出色、富有、受人尊敬，最终仍然失去对自己所造之物的控制。AI 并没有制造这种不稳定，只是让它在职业生涯中更早显形。代价是：把身份从成就上松开，并不能告诉一个人在工作消失之后如何过好每一天。

quote.en: For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?
quote.zh: 人在日光之下劳碌累心，所得的是什么呢？

origin.zh: 犹地亚，约公元前 3 世纪

label.en: Ecclesiastes 2:22, King James Version
label.zh: 《传道书》2:22，钦定本

claim.en: I argued that when workers lose control over their own activity and its product, they lose more than pay: they are estranged from themselves, because shaping the world is how human beings confirm what they are.
claim.zh: 我论证过，当工人失去了对自身活动及其产品的支配，他们失去的不只是报酬，而是与自身相疏离，因为人正是通过改造世界来确认自己是什么。

detail.en: Marx's charge against industrial work was never only low pay. When control over productive activity is taken from the person doing it, alienation follows. AI could rebuild the same problem in a new shape: society still makes extraordinary things, and fewer and fewer people experience themselves as necessary to making them. Preserving inefficient jobs would not answer him either.
detail.zh: 马克思对工业劳动的指控从来不只是工资低。当一个人对自己生产活动的控制被拿走，异化随之而来。AI 可能以新的形式重建同一个问题：社会依然造出非凡的东西，而越来越少的人觉得自己是其中必要的一环。仅仅保留低效的岗位，同样回答不了他。

quote.en: The worker therefore only feels himself outside his work, and in his work feels outside himself.
quote.zh: 因此，工人只有在工作之外才感到自在，而在工作之中却感到不自在。

label.en: Karl Marx, Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, "Estranged Labour"
label.zh: 卡尔·马克思《1844 年经济学哲学手稿》〈异化劳动〉

claim.en: I argued that a lasting peace could not rest on pleasure alone: people need arenas that call on hardihood and discipline, and I proposed finding a moral equivalent for what war had demanded of them.
claim.zh: 我论证过，持久的和平不能只建立在享乐之上：人需要召唤坚韧与纪律的场域，所以我提议为战争曾经对人提出的要求，找一个道德上的替代。

detail.en: James doubted that a society organised purely for ease could hold. Applied to AI, removing difficult intellectual work may free us, but a world in which nothing calls on our persistence or competence also removes the occasions through which people find out what they can do. This is not an argument for keeping unnecessary jobs — it is an argument for deliberately making new arenas when the old ones close.
detail.zh: 詹姆斯怀疑一个纯粹为舒适而组织起来的社会能否维持。应用到 AI：取消困难的智力劳动也许让人自由，但一个没有任何事情要求毅力与能力的世界，也取消了人借以发现自己能做什么的场合。这不是主张保留不必要的岗位，而是主张在旧场域关闭时，刻意去造出新的。

quote.en: A permanently successful peace-economy can not be a simple pleasure-economy.
quote.zh: 一个能够长久成立的和平经济，不可能只是一种享乐经济。

label.en: William James, "The Moral Equivalent of War", 1910
label.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯〈战争的道德等价物〉，1910 年

claim.en: I wrote that outward things cannot touch the soul, which turns and moves itself. What is most mine is the part that examines my impulses and decides how to answer them.
claim.zh: 我写过，外物触碰不到灵魂，灵魂只由它自己转动。最属于我的，是那个审视冲动、决定如何回应它们的部分。

detail.en: A Stoic reading creates a reason to be suspicious when a drug changes desire itself: fewer cravings may make life easier without necessarily revealing a truer character. The cost is that this draws a sharp line between reason and bodily states even though modern neuroscience shows that judgment and motivation are themselves embodied.
detail.zh: 从斯多葛主义出发，当一种药直接改变欲望本身时，我们有理由保持警惕：欲望减少可能让生活更轻松，却不一定代表一个更真实的性格。这个立场的代价是，它把理性与身体状态分得很开，而现代神经科学恰恰显示，判断和动机本身也依赖身体。

quote.en: Things themselves touch not the soul, not in the least degree; nor have they admission to the soul, nor can they turn or move the soul: but the soul turns and moves itself alone.
quote.zh: 事物本身完全触碰不到灵魂，它们进不了灵魂，也无法扭转或推动灵魂；灵魂只由它自己扭转、自己推动。

label.en: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, Book V, §19, trans. George Long
label.zh: 马可·奥勒留《沉思录》第五卷第 19 节，朗 英译

claim.en: I held that a person should become what he is, and need not stay loyal to an earlier self just because it came first. What matters is becoming a self one can affirm.
claim.zh: 我认为，人应当成为他之所是，而不必只因为过去的自己先出现，就一直忠于它。要紧的是成为一个自己能够肯定的人。

detail.en: A GLP-1 can make this uncomfortable because self-transformation is no longer achieved only through discipline, experience or struggle; chemistry can participate too. The price of this view is accepting that intentionally changing desire may count as self-creation rather than corruption of an original self.
detail.zh: GLP-1 让这个问题变得不舒服，是因为人的改变不再只能通过自律、经历或挣扎完成，化学也可以参与其中。接受这个立场意味着：主动改变自己的欲望，也可能属于自我塑造，而不是对原本自我的破坏。

quote.en: What saith thy conscience?—'Thou shalt become what thou art.'
quote.zh: 你的良心说什么？——「你应当成为你之所是。」

label.en: Friedrich Nietzsche, The Joyful Wisdom, §270, trans. Thomas Common
label.zh: 弗里德里希·尼采《快乐的科学》第 270 节，康芒 英译

claim.en: I argued that a person first exists and only afterwards defines himself by what he does. There is no finished nature inside to protect; I am what I make of the conditions I am given.
claim.zh: 我主张，人先存在，然后才通过自己的行动来定义自己。里面并没有一个现成的本性需要保护；我是我对所处条件的作为。

detail.en: Sartre makes the question 'Which version was there first?' much less important. If medication changes the field in which you make choices, the harder question becomes whether you take responsibility for the life you construct with that changed condition.
detail.zh: 萨特会让哪个版本先出现这件事变得没那么重要。如果药物改变了你做选择时所处的心理条件，更困难的问题反而是：你是否愿意为自己在这个新条件下创造出来的生活负责。

quote.en: Man first of all exists, encounters himself, surges up in the world – and defines himself afterwards.
quote.zh: 人首先存在，遇见自己，在世界中涌现 — 然后才定义自己。

label.en: Jean-Paul Sartre, Existentialism is a Humanism, 1946
label.zh: 让-保罗·萨特《存在主义是一种人道主义》，1946 年

claim.en: I looked inward for a self beneath my perceptions and never found one. Each time I caught only some particular perception, never myself without it.
claim.zh: 我向内寻找知觉之下的自我，却从未找到。每一次我捕捉到的都只是某个具体的知觉，从来不是没有知觉的我自己。

detail.en: On this view, GLP-1 does not replace a true personality with a fake one; it changes some of the perceptions and motivations making up the current person. The unsettling cost is that there may be no final baseline to which you can return and say, 'This one was really me.'
detail.zh: 按照这种理解，GLP-1 并不是用一个假的人格替换真正的人格，而只是改变了组成当前这个人的部分感受和动机。令人不安的代价是：也许根本不存在一个最终基准，让你可以回去指着它说，这个才是真正的我。

quote.en: I never can catch myself at any time without a perception, and never can observe any thing but the perception.
quote.zh: 我从来不能在没有任何知觉的时候捕捉到自己，也从来观察不到知觉之外的任何东西。

label.en: David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book I, Part IV, §VI
label.zh: 大卫·休谟《人性论》第一卷第四部分第六节

claim.en: We teach that body, feeling, perception, formations and consciousness are each impermanent and not-self. No permanent owner stands behind these changing states.
claim.zh: 我们教导：色、受、想、行、识，每一样都是无常的，都不是我。这些变化的状态背后，并没有一个永恒的主人。

detail.en: Early Buddhist teaching treats bodily form, feeling, perception, volitional formations and consciousness as impermanent and not-self. A drug changing craving is therefore another striking demonstration that desires arise from conditions; the cost is giving up the comforting idea that your untreated desires reveal an essential identity.
detail.zh: 早期佛教把色、受、想、行、识都看作无常、非我。药物能够改变渴望，反而非常直接地展示了欲望依条件而生；这个观点的代价，是放弃一个很令人安心的想法 — 未经药物影响的欲望能够揭示一个本质性的自我。

quote.en: This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.
quote.zh: 这不是我的，这不是我，这不是我的自我。

origin.zh: 印度，约公元前 5 世纪

label.en: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.59, Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta, trans. Bhikkhu Bodhi (Pali: netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā)
label.zh: 《相应部》22.59〈无我相经〉，菩提比丘 英译（巴利原文：netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā）

claim.en: I argued against judging a state of mind by its bodily origin. Every feeling has a physical cause; a state should be judged by its fruits in a life, not by its roots.
claim.zh: 我反对按身体来源去评判一种心理状态。每种感受都有生理原因；评判它应看它在生活中结出的果实，而不是它的根。

detail.en: James made this argument against what he called medical materialism: explaining an experience through nerves, disease or physiology does not settle its value. Applied to GLP-1, discovering that calmness or reduced craving comes from a receptor agonist tells us how the change happened, not whether the resulting life is better, worse or more authentic.
detail.zh: 詹姆斯用这个观点反对他所谓的医学唯物主义：即使我们能够用神经、疾病或生理机制解释一种体验，也不能因此决定它的价值。应用到 GLP-1，知道平静或欲望降低来自受体激动剂，只能解释变化是怎么发生的，并不能回答改变后的生活更好、更坏，还是更真实。

quote.en: By their fruits ye shall know them, not by their roots.
quote.zh: 看它们结出的果实来认识它们，而不是看它们的根。

label.en: William James, The Varieties of Religious Experience, Lecture I: Religion and Neurology
label.zh: 威廉·詹姆斯《宗教经验之种种》第一讲「宗教与神经学」

claim.en: I argued that a person is sovereign over his own body and mind, and that preventing harm to others is the only rightful reason to override his choice. Disgust, or a belief that it is for his own good, is not enough.
claim.zh: 我主张，一个人对自己的身体和心灵拥有主权；违背他的意愿加以干涉，唯一正当的理由是防止他伤害别人。别人的厌恶，或者认为这是为他好，都不够。

detail.en: Mill's principle strongly protects voluntary bodily choices, but it contains its own limit: harm to others. The unresolved question is whether exploitation of donors or consequences for donor-conceived children count as enough harm to justify restrictions.
detail.zh: 密尔的原则强烈保护成年人自愿支配身体的选择，但它本身也有一个边界：对他人的伤害。因此真正的争议是，捐赠者受到经济剥削、或通过捐赠出生的孩子所受到的影响，是否已经构成足够的伤害来限制这种自由。

quote.en: Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign.
quote.zh: 对于他自己，对于他自己的身体和心灵，个人是最高主权者。

label.en: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty, Chapter I
label.zh: 约翰·斯图亚特·密尔《论自由》第一章

claim.en: I observed that we get what we need from strangers by appealing to their self-love, not their kindness. Exchange lets people cooperate because each side gains something it values.
claim.zh: 我观察到，我们从陌生人那里得到所需，靠的是诉诸他们的自利，而不是他们的仁慈。交换让人们能够合作，因为双方都得到了自己看重的东西。

detail.en: Smith gives the strongest economic intuition behind a legal market: recipients want scarce reproductive material and donors bear time, inconvenience or risk. But his argument about exchange does not establish that everything people value should be for sale, so regulation remains an open question.
detail.zh: 斯密提供了支持合法市场最直接的经济逻辑：接受者需要稀缺的生殖材料，而捐赠者承担时间、不便甚至风险。但交换能够互利，并不能证明所有有价值的东西都应该自由出售，因此监管问题仍然存在。

quote.en: We address ourselves, not to their humanity, but to their self-love, and never talk to them of our own necessities, but of their advantages.
quote.zh: 我们不是诉诸他们的仁慈，而是诉诸他们的自利；我们从不向他们诉说自己的需要，而只谈他们的利益。

label.en: Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, Book I, Chapter II
label.zh: 亚当·斯密《国富论》第一卷第二章

claim.en: I taught that the body, like property and reputation, is not within our control; only our own judgments and actions are. Whoever treats the body as wholly his own has mistaken where his freedom lies.
claim.zh: 我教导说，身体和财产、名声一样，不在我们的掌控之内；只有我们自己的判断和行动才是。把身体当作完全属于自己的人，弄错了自由所在的地方。

detail.en: A Stoic approach would put less moral weight on maximizing what the body can earn and more on whether the choice is deliberate and consistent with character. That points toward permission with safeguards rather than treating reproductive material as an ordinary unrestricted commodity.
detail.zh: 斯多葛主义不会把重点放在身体能够卖多少钱，而更关注一个选择是否经过理性判断、是否符合一个人的品格。这更接近允许交易但设置保护，而不是把生殖材料当作完全不受限制的普通商品。

quote.en: Things not in our control are body, property, reputation, command, and, in one word, whatever are not our own actions.
quote.zh: 不在我们控制之中的，是身体、财产、名声、权位，总之，是一切并非我们自己行为的东西。

origin.zh: 尼科波利斯，约公元 125 年

label.en: Epictetus, Enchiridion §1, trans. Elizabeth Carter
label.zh: 爱比克泰德《手册》第 1 节，卡特 英译

claim.en: I argued that what is shared by the greatest number receives the least care, because each person attends chiefly to what is his own. Responsibility needs someone it clearly belongs to.
claim.zh: 我论证过，被最多人共有的东西，得到的照料最少，因为每个人主要关心属于自己的东西。责任需要一个明确归属的人。

detail.en: Aristotle was discussing common families and property, not gamete markets, so this is an application of his argument rather than his view on sperm or eggs. His warning matters here because donors, clinics, intended parents and future children create overlapping responsibilities that a simple buyer-seller contract may not settle.
detail.zh: 亚里士多德讨论的是共有家庭和财产，并不是精子或卵子市场，因此这里是在应用他的原则，而不是声称他讨论过现代辅助生殖。他的警告仍然相关：捐赠者、诊所、准父母和未来的孩子之间存在重叠责任，一张简单的买卖合同未必能够解决。

quote.en: For that which is common to the greatest number has the least care bestowed upon it.
quote.zh: 由最多人共同拥有的东西，往往得到最少的照料。

label.en: Aristotle, Politics, Book II, Chapter III, 1261b, trans. Benjamin Jowett
label.zh: 亚里士多德《政治学》第二卷第三章 1261b，乔伊特 英译

claim.en: I taught that the noble person is guided by what is right and the petty person by what is profitable. Gain should never be the first question.
claim.zh: 我教导说，君子以义为准，小人以利为准。利益永远不应该是首先要问的问题。
